title: Plan children’s rooms around activities
intro: Plan a room for two school-age children around sleeping, playing, studying and storage. Coordinate movement, foreseeable hazards and changing needs rather than beginning with a colour theme.

sections.title: Define both children’s activity needs
sections.text: Record each child’s activities, schedules, belongings and assistance needs. Similar ages do not establish identical reach or preferences. Separate shared and personal areas. This project concerns school-age users; infant and toddler sleeping products require distinct classifications and requirements. Turn the family’s brief into a reviewable programme before choosing a furniture arrangement.
sections.caption: Individual needs first, then shared-space decisions.

sections.title: Connect zones and review hazards
sections.text: Connect sleeping, study, play and storage zones to the entrance and open furniture states. Review services, window coverings and objects that encourage climbing. CPSC advises securing furniture/TVs according to manufacturer instructions and removing tempting objects from their tops. A layout does not replace appropriate product selection, assembly and substrate-specific installation review.
sections.caption: Review routes, open states and climbing incentives together.

sections.title: Plan growth without improvised conversion
sections.text: Identify changes supported by the product: content rearrangement, a designed adjustable shelf or relocating a unit with renewed restraint review. Distinguish these from modifying a bed or adding an unapproved mechanism. Document a future arrangement and its rechecks rather than promising one piece for every age. Preserve openings and useful shared space after changes.
sections.caption: Adapt within the product’s permitted configuration and recheck changes.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: One child studies while the other plays. Option A places the occupied chair in the entrance route; B relocates study and retains a clear route and personal storage. Develop B, test opening states and review storage restraint against the selected product instructions.
example.decision: Decision: verify simultaneous tasks, access and hazard controls before acceptance.

quiz.question: Do similar ages prove identical needs?
options: No; review each child and their use
quiz.explanation: Activities, reach, assistance and schedules can differ despite similar ages.

assignment.prompt: Prepare individual briefs, two layouts, a simultaneous-use case and a permitted future adaptation.

faq.question: Can the same school-age brief be used for an infant?
faq.answer: No. Users, sleeping-product categories and their requirements differ and need a separate review.
